card.description:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
 
 
Department: EHSQ / Quality
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
 
 
Direct Reports: None
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
 
 
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on BESS scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers both standalone BESS facilities and BESS integrated with utility-scale solar PV projects.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active BESS construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of BESS Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of utility-scale BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, power conversion systems (PCS) and inverters, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary power, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection, suppression, gas detection, and explosion control installation interfaces. Equally important is a working command of manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements, which often govern acceptance more directly than the project drawings. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, battery management and energy management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing remain with Engineering, Commissioning, and the manufacturer; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on standalone and PV-integrated BESS construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for BESS scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain BESS inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing BESS scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying BESS-specific contract, manufacturer, testing, and authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the BESS Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, manufacturer requirements, documentation requirements, and common BESS failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the BESS Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for BESS scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering and the manufacturer.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring BESS nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, subcontractor, or manufacturer personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of BESS equipment, including manufacturer limits on storage conditions, storage duration, and state-of-charge maintenance that affect product conformity and warranty.
* Verify that manufacturer installation checklists, field service requirements, and warranty-related documentation are integrated into ITPs and completed in sequence, and coordinate Quality activities with manufacturer field representatives.
* Review pre-commissioning and construction test records, including torque verification, insulation resistance, and continuity testing, for completeness and conformance with project specifications, manufacturer requirements, and ANSI/NETA ATS where applicable.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in mechanical completion, energization-readiness, and turnover verification for BESS systems, while maintaining clear separation from battery management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of BESS enclosures, PCS, and transformers, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with owner’s engineers, independent engineers, AHJs, fire officials, and third-party agencies on BESS Quality matters, including inspection and documentation requirements associated with fire and life-safety systems.
* Align closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects and manufacturers.
* Monitor BESS Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the BESS Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation, including manufacturer and warranty records.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, BESS, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, code, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, manufacturers, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships with project teams and manufacturers.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, manufacturer responsibilities, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, preservation records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, manufacturers, owners, AHJs, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, or industrial construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on utility-scale BESS projects; utility-scale PV experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for BESS construction.
* Strong working knowledge of BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, PCS and inverter equipment, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary systems, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection and suppression installation interfaces.
* Demonstrated experience applying manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements for utility-scale energy storage equipment.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, single-line diagrams, equipment layouts, grounding plans, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer installation manuals.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted BESS work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with manufacturer field representatives, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and AHJs.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, manufacturer, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners (NABCEP): Energy Storage Installation Professional (ESIP) or PV Installation Professional (PVIP)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ Manufacturer credentials: Installation or field service certification on one or more utility-scale BESS platforms
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of BESS enclosures, PCS, or transformers.
* Experience across multiple BESS manufacturers, battery technologies, PCS platforms, thermal management designs, and both AC-coupled and DC-coupled configurations.
* Working knowledge of NFPA 855, NEC (NFPA 70) Article 706, UL 9540 and UL 9540A, and the energy storage provisions of the International Fire Code.
* Experience supporting BESS mechanical completion, construction completion, or commissioning-readiness documentation.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV, medium-voltage collection, or substation scopes adjacent to BESS installations.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, manufacturers, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access BESS enclosures and equipment areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access BESS and electrical construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, BESS-specific hazard controls, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale BESS, solar, and substation construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized equipment and stored-energy hazards as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, BESS hazard controls, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, manufacturer availability, testing schedules, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.

Hanwha Qcells is proud to be an at-will Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination against race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, citizenship, disability, protected veteran status and any other classification protected by applicable federal, state or local law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
 
 
We are committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Hanwha Qcells will provide reasonable accommodations to all qualified individuals with disabilities to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodations at hr-usa@qcells.com.
 
 
Nothing in this statement shall imply implicitly or explicitly a guarantee of employment outside our at-will employment opportunity.

card.title: Quality Technical Director
card.description:
Own the division’s quality strategy end-to-end, ensuring product safety, laboratory operations, manufacturing processes, customer support, and compliance work together to protect quality and meet regulatory expectations.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Set technical and quality direction, translating business goals into practical standards, processes, and performance measures across the value chain.
* Build and lead a high-performing quality organization, coaching teams in root-cause problem solving, risk management, and documentation discipline.
* Strengthen supplier quality through performance reviews, issue containment expectations, and clear escalation paths.
* Lead investigation and resolution of customer quality issues, coordinating internal stakeholders to deliver effective corrective and preventive actions.
* Drive continuous improvement to enhance product performance and operational effectiveness, identifying systemic gaps and verifying outcomes.

**What You Bring**
Deep experience in quality systems and product safety, strong technical leadership, and a pragmatic approach to compliance and cross-functional execution—able to turn complex investigations into durable improvements.

card.title: Senior Director, Master Data Management & Operations
card.description:
Join the team behind iconic brands like Huggies®, Kleenex®, Cottonelle®, Scott®, Kotex®, Poise®, Depend®, and Kimberly-Clark Professional®. At Kimberly-Clark, it’s all here for you—innovation, growth, and the chance to make a real impact.
 
 
**Led by Purpose. Driven by You.**

 
 

The Senior Director, Master Data Management & Operations (MDM) will lead the enterprise master data capability. They will establish clear ownership and operating discipline so that critical business data is accurate, trusted, and ready to support the business.

 

Reporting to the VP Data & AI, the Senior Director, MDM will lead a global team of 65 with three direct reports focused on 1) functional data domains 2) engineering and tooling 3) supporting transformation and operations.

 

This leader will play a central role in a multi-year enterprise transformation and integration agenda, ensuring master data is ready to support major system and business changes. They will balance near-term delivery priorities with the long-term target state, while supporting existing systems alongside modern governance platforms; as well as focus on:

 

* **End to End master data ownership**: Own master data across all functions, regions, and business segments. Establish clear accountability, decision rights, and drive decisions and escalations.
 

* **Integration and program delivery**: Lead master data readiness for large-scale enterprise integration and transformation efforts. This includes integration experience, comfort operating at scale in a matrix, and the ability to influence senior business leaders across the company.
 

**Role & Responsibilities**
 
The Senior Director, MDM serves as a key transformational leader who will be responsible for:

**Enterprise Master Data Strategy**

* Define and own the enterprise master data strategy, setting a clear direction for how master data will be owned, governed, and used to run the business with confidence.
* Establish the operating model and talent strategy needed to manage master data end to end.
* Partner with business and technology leaders to align priorities, investments, and capabilities to enterprise objectives.
* Serve as the single point of accountability for master data, translating data strategy into measurable business outcomes.
 

**Engineering & Tooling Ownership**

* Own the master data engineering and tooling agenda, setting the target-state architecture and roadmap for master data platforms, integrations, and supporting tools.
* Drive standardization and simplification of the master data tooling landscape, rationalizing redundant and legacy tools in favor of common enterprise platforms.
* Use tooling to drive efficiency, consistency, and simplification of master data processes, embedding standards, data quality rules, and governance directly into the workflow.
Drive intelligent automation of master data processes, applying workflow automation, AI, and machine learning to reduce manual effort, accelerate cycle times, and improve data quality. 

**Enterprise Integration & Transformation**

* Lead master data readiness for large-scale enterprise integration and transformation programs.
* Oversee master data enablement for ERP transformation, including harmonization, integration, and migration efforts.
* Balance near-term delivery priorities with the long-term target state.
Support existing systems alongside modern governance platforms as the enterprise transitions. 

**Business Partnership & Influence**

* Collaborate with senior business and technology leaders across the enterprise to align master data capabilities to critical business domains.
Influence in a matrix environment, driving decisions and escalations rather than acting as a subject matter expert or order taker. 

**Functional Leadership**

* Develop a global, multi-disciplinary team spanning domain ownership, technology and tooling, and program operations.
* Coach and mentor leaders, attracting top talent and creating an environment where data professionals do their best work.
Integrate teams and capabilities through shared priorities, standards, and operating rhythms. 

**Experience We're Looking For:** 
 
The Senior Director, MDM will have a proven track record leading master data at large, global organizations, with deep expertise across master data management, data quality, stewardship, governance, integration, and data product ownership. This leader will ideally bring experience in CPG or adjacent, complex consumer-oriented industries such as Pharmaceuticals, Retail, or Manufacturing, including exposure to regulated or restricted products. Experience in mergers, acquisitions, and large-scale enterprise integration is highly valued. Familiarity with enterprise ERP environments and modern master data governance platforms is helpful.

Equally important is the ability to operate as a strategic, influential leader who can partner with senior business and technology leaders, drive decisions and escalations, and influence in a large, matrixed organization. The Senior Director, MDM will be comfortable with complexity and change, able to set clear direction for a global team. They will bring strong execution, attention to detail, and a collaborative, action-oriented leadership style, with a record of building, coaching, and mentoring high-performing teams.

**Functional Skills & Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience, including accountability for complex, end-to-end master data in large, matrixed enterprises.
* Deep expertise in master data management, governance, data quality, stewardship, standards, and adoption.
* Proven success owning master data end to end across functions, regions, and business segments.
* Experience leading M&A, enterprise integration, and ERP-enabled master data harmonization, migration, and consolidation.
* Demonstrated success establishing data product ownership models with clearly defined domain owners.
* Experience in CPG or adjacent, complex consumer-oriented industries, such as Pharmaceuticals, Retail, or Manufacturing, including exposure to regulated or restricted products.
* Familiarity with enterprise ERP environments and modern master data governance platforms.
* Experience supporting legacy and multi-region systems alongside modern governance platforms during a multi-year transition.
* Track record leading global, geographically dispersed teams through significant integration, transformation, and ambiguity.
* Proven ability to deliver near-term program priorities while executing against a long-term target state.
 

 

**Leadership Capabilities**·
 
**Strategic influence:** Operates as a strategic leader with gravitas who can partner with senior business and technology leaders and influence decisions.
 
 
**Enterprise transformation leadership:** Sets clear direction and turns strategy into disciplined execution across people, processes, and technology.
 
 
**Operating at scale:** Works effectively in large, matrixed environments where master data touches every function, region, and segment.
 
 
**Execution orientation:** Brings strong execution and attention to detail, with a record of delivering against complex, multi-year programs.

 

**Collaborative, action-oriented style:** Works well with a collaborative leadership team and adds an accountable, execution-focused approach.

 

**Talent and culture leadership:** Attracts and develops strong talent, inspires high-performing teams, and unites newly formed organizations around shared priorities, decision rights, operating rhythms, and ways of working.
 
 
**Education Credentials** 
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, data science, information systems, technology, or related discipline required. MBA or advanced degree is an added benefit.
 
 
**Total Benefits** 
 
We believe that our employees are our greatest asset, and we're committed to providing them with the resources they need to be successful. If you're looking for a rewarding career with a company that cares about its employees, then Kimberly-Clark is the place for you.
 
 
Here are just a few of the benefits you’d enjoy working in this role for Kimberly-Clark. For a complete overview, see www.mykcbenefits.com .
 
 
**To Be Considered** 
 
Click the Apply button and complete the online application process. A member of our recruiting team will review your application and follow up if you seem like a great fit for this role.
 
 
In the meantime, please check out the careers website.
 
 
**And finally, the fine print….**

*For Kimberly-Clark to grow and prosper, we must be an inclusive organization that applies the diverse experiences and passions of its team members to brands that make life better for people all around the world, which is why we seek to build a workforce that encompasses the experiences of our consumers. When you bring your original thinking to Kimberly-Clark, you fuel the continued success of our enterprise. We are a committed equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, pregnancy, genetic information, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by law.* 
 
*The statements above are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this classification. Statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and skills required for this position.* 
 
*Employment is subject to verification of local policies.* 
 
*Employment is subject to verification of pre-screening tests which may include drug screening, background check, and DMV check.* 
 
*Veterans and members of the Reserve and Guard are highly encouraged to apply.*

Salary Range: 221,300 – 286,100 USD

At Kimberly-Clark, pay is just one aspect of our total rewards package, which also includes a variety of benefits and opportunities to achieve, thrive and grow. Along with base pay, this position offers eligibility for a target bonus and a comprehensive benefits suite, including our 401(k) and Profit Sharing plan. The anticipated base pay range for this role is provided above for a fully qualified hire. Actual pay will depend on several factors, such as location, role, skills, performance, and experience. Please note that the stated pay range applies to US locations only.

card.title: Director Destination Care Operations
card.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high-quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Establishes and maintains documentation standards and data integrity practices across the team to support accurate program reporting, operational decision-making, and continuity of patient care. Serves as the escalation point for the team and provides availability for complex or time-sensitive situations as they arise. Manages the destination care program budget and is accountable for financial performance against established targets.
* Sets clear performance expectations, invests in professional growth, and builds and sustains a high-performing team culture grounded in service excellence, operational consistency, and continuous improvement; establishes clear standards and ensures consistent adherence across the team, addressing performance gaps directly and constructively.
* Oversees onboarding, cross-training, and workflow consistency across the program. Leads change management efforts within the team to support adoption of new workflows, service standards, and program initiatives.

**Job Requirements**

Required

* Bachelors Other Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field. and 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, upon hire and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patient populations, including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary or quaternary care settings, upon hire and
* Experience with electronic health record and hospital information systems; proficiency with productivity suites including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office., upon hire or

Preferred

* Masters Other Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nursing, or a related field and 7-9 years 7 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience with international patient programs, embassy-sponsored care, or global sponsor coordination., upon hire and
* Clinical background including Registered Nurse (RN) licensure or equivalent clinical operations experience, upon hire and
* Experience in a dedicated destination care, international patient services, or specialty referral program at an academic medical center or large health system, upon hire and
* Experience building or expanding programs, including policy and operational protocol development, upon hire and
* Experience preparing and delivering financial and operating performance reports and presentations for leadership, upon hire and
* Experience with referral management, patient access, financial counseling, registration, or admissions workflows, upon hire and
* Experience managing program operations across multiple facilities or markets within a large health system., upon hire
* Certified Case Manager, upon hire or
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification, upon hire or
* Project Management Professional, upon hire or
* Registered Nurse: TX, upon hire

Where You'll Work

Baylor St. Luke’s Medical Center is an 1,045 bed facility located in the Texas medical center. A joint venture with Baylor College of Medicine, Baylor St. Luke’s is an internationally recognized leader in research and clinical excellence that has given rise to breakthroughs in cardiovascular care, neuroscience, oncology, transplantation, and more. The hospital is home to the Dan L Duncan Comprehensive Cancer Center, a nationally-accredited and NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Our new McNair Campus is designed around the human experience—modeled on evidence-based practices for the safety of patients, visitors, staff, and physicians. The 27.5-acre campus represents the future of healthcare through a transformative alliance focused on leading-edge patient care, research, and education.

 **Pay Range** 
$60.24 - $89.60 /hour

card.title: Executive Vice President, Head of Commercial Access & Operations
card.description:
***ABOUT MEITHEAL PHARMACEUTICALS***

*Founded in 2017 and based in Chicago, Meitheal is focused on the development and commercialization of generic injectable medications and, as of 2022, has expanded its focus to include fertility, biologic, and branded products. Meitheal currently markets over 75 U.S. FDA-approved products across numerous therapeutic areas including anti-infectives, oncolytics, intensive care, and fertility. As of April 2026, Meitheal, directly or through its partners, has 32 products in the research and development phase, 9 products planned for launch in 2026, 4 products in clinical trial phases, and 13 products under review by the FDA. Meitheal’s mission is to provide easy access to fairly priced products through robust manufacturing, consistent supply, and rapid response to our customers’ needs. Ranked regularly as one of Crain’s Fast 50 in Chicago, and in the top 100 of Crain’s Best Places to Work in Chicago from 2022 to 2026, Meitheal emulates the traditional Irish guiding principle we are named for—working together toward a common goal, for the greater good.*

*Learn more about who we are and what we do at* *www.meithealpharma.com**.*

***The pay range for this position is $350,000 to $425,000 / year. Payrate is determined by considering a person's prior experience and competence.***

*The estimated salary range reflects an anticipated range for this position. The actual base salary offered may depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. The actual base salary offered will be in accordance with state or local minimum wage requirements for the job location.*

***What We Offer***

* *Competitive pay and medical, dental, and vision insurance*
* *Flexible spending accounts*
* *Long- and short-term disability insurance, as well as life insurance*
* *401(k) plan with match*
* *Competitive PTO and company-paid holidays*
* *Paid parental leave (maternity & paternity)*
* *Employee assistance program*
* *Onsite Gym*

**Summary**

Meitheal Pharmaceuticals is seeking an experienced, commercially focused Executive Vice President, Head of Commercial Access & Operations to lead U.S. market access strategy and commercial operating execution in support of its growing biosimilar portfolio and, as assigned, other Company businesses. This executive will be accountable for payer and channel access, pricing and contracting strategy and execution, commercial launch operational readiness jointly with the EVP, distribution and specialty channel execution, commercial analytics, and operational performance. Product launch strategy is developed and governed cross-functionally across the Company, with the executive leading its market access and commercial operations components. The role requires senior-level relationships with payers, PBMs, GPOs, specialty pharmacies, and distributors, combined with the ability to build disciplined, scalable commercial processes. The position leads the commercial access and operations functions assigned to it and partners with the SVP of Specialty and VP of Biosimilars & Women’s Health on portfolio priorities and commercialization.

**Essential Responsibilities**

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

**Market Access, Pricing & Contracting**

* Develop and execute U.S. market access strategies across pharmacy and medical benefits, retail, specialty, and institutional channels, aligned with cross-functional product and portfolio strategies.
* Lead payer, PBM, health plan, GPO, and strategic account negotiations within approved contracting authority and in coordination with designated business-unit and customer relationship owners to secure favorable formulary positioning, reimbursement, utilization, and profitable access.
* Lead the development and execution of pricing, rebate, contracting, preferred placement, step-therapy, and other compliant access strategies, subject to established pricing, profitability, Legal/Compliance, and executive approval authorities.
* Monitor payer policy, reimbursement trends, competitive launches, and biosimilar adoption to refine commercial plans.

**Commercial Operations & Channel Execution**

* Jointly lead commercial launch operational readiness with including market access, customer onboarding, distribution setup, contract implementation, and operational milestones, as part of the Company’s cross-functional product launch strategy and governance.
* Oversee designated commercial channel relationships and operating performance with wholesalers, specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, and other channel partners, coordinating with existing relationship owners and Supply Chain.
* Establish effective contract implementation, administration, customer reporting, and performance monitoring processes, in partnership with Finance, Legal, and other functional owners.
* Develop scalable commercial processes, systems requirements, dashboards, and governance for forecasting, demand planning inputs, customer performance, and issue resolution.
* Partner with Supply Chain to align commercial demand, inventory availability, service levels, and customer commitments.
* Ensure market access, contracting, distribution, and channel practices are developed and implemented in coordination with Legal, Compliance, Regulatory, and Finance, including applicable government pricing and pharmaceutical compliance requirements.

**Financial Performance & Business Insights**

* Establish and monitor commercial access and operations KPIs, including preferred access, contract performance, channel utilization, operational launch milestones, and the impact of access and channel strategies on net revenue and profitability.
* Partner with Finance and designated business-unit leaders on product-level P&L reviews, revenue forecasts, gross-to-net assumptions, rebate accrual inputs, contribution margin, and budget discipline; product-level P&L accountability remains with the designated business owner.
* Provide cross-functional recommendations on portfolio and product profitability decisions, including pricing trade-offs, channel mix, contract economics, launch investments, and resource allocation; material decisions remain subject to established Company approval authority.

**Executive Leadership & Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Build and lead the commercial access and operations functions assigned to this role, with clear decision rights, functional accountability, and collaborative processes aligned to portfolio scale and launch priorities.
* Coordinate with Specialty and other business-unit leaders, the EVP, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure compliant and effective execution.
* Participate in cross-functional business reviews with Finance, Supply Chain, and portfolio leaders to assess performance against product P&L plans, identify variances and corrective actions, and present commercial recommendations to executive leadership.
* Escalate unresolved disagreements over product priorities, customer ownership, pricing economics, or operational execution through the Company’s established cross-functional governance and executive decision-making processes.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly oversee team responsible for Commercial Access and Operations
* Provides leadership, coaching, performance management, and strategic direction for growth of biosimilar portfolio

**Core Competencies**

* Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
* Strategic thinker with outstanding analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to engage internal and external stakeholders, and commercial teams.
* Strong operational execution, balancing high-level strategic vision with hands-on leadership.
* Comprehensive knowledge of regulatory requirements, compliance, and industry standards.

**Qualifications**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Required: Direct, substantive Medical Affairs leadership experience with biosimilars, including at least one U.S. biosimilar launch or significant prelaunch commercialization program.
* Required: Working knowledge of FDA biosimilar regulatory pathways, interchangeability, extrapolation, immunogenicity, and scientific communication to healthcare professionals.
* Strongly preferred: Experience supporting biosimilar formulary adoption, payer evidence needs, provider switching education, and collaboration with Market Access.

**Education and/or Experience Required**

* MD, PhD, or PharmD required.
* Minimum 15+ years of experience in Pharma/Biotech, 10+ years Medical Affairs department, including leadership roles in biotech/pharmaceutical companies.

**Computer Skills**

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including PowerPoint, Word, Excel, and Outlook.

**Physical Demands**

* While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit and talk or hear.
* The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.

**Work Environment**

* The ability to travel up to 40%, including overnights, as dictated by business need and attend all company sponsored events/meetings/conferences.
* Field-base Role/Remote.

***AAP/EEO***

*Meitheal Pharmaceuticals is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including minorities, women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities.*

card.title: Director of Practice and ASC Operations
card.description:
**Director of Practice and ASC Operations**

Reporting to: Chief Operating Officer

**About the Role**

Lead the day-to-day business operations of a multi-provider pain management practice and ambulatory surgery center (ASC). Your initial priorities will be to make it easier for patients and referring offices to reach us, convert more referrals into scheduled visits, and make better use of clinic and procedure capacity.

**A core part of the role is using data, technology, and automation to improve how the practice and ASC operate as they grow.** You’ll use call, referral, and scheduling data to see where patients get stuck and where capacity goes unused. You’ll then redesign workflows, improve how teams use existing systems, and automate repetitive steps such as routing callbacks or flagging referrals that need follow-up. You’ll measure whether those changes improve access, reduce manual work, and free up staff time.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll lead staff, set clear expectations, and work directly with physicians and the ASC Director of Nursing to improve how the practice and surgery center operate. We welcome leaders from healthcare and other complex service businesses. You’ll bring experience leading a team, using data to identify problems, and carrying changes through to measurable results.

**What You Bring**

**Required**

* Progressive operations leadership experience with direct responsibility for hiring, coaching, developing, and managing the performance of a team.
* Experience running a complex, customer-facing operation and managing the drivers of financial performance, such as labor, capacity, productivity, and operating expenses.
* A track record of personally leading workflow improvements that produced measurable, sustained results in access, service, efficiency, or cost.
* Experience using data and KPIs to identify bottlenecks, prioritize action, and verify that changes improved performance.
* Experience using technology or automation to simplify workflows, reduce manual work, and help staff adopt new ways of working.
* Ability to lead changes that span teams, take ownership when progress stalls, and work hands-on with frontline staff to resolve problems.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

**What success looks like**

* **Better patient access.** Make it easier for patients to connect with us and stay engaged throughout their care. Answer more calls live, return messages promptly, and offer convenient online scheduling for eligible visits. Use technology alongside personal outreach to keep patients informed, respond to their needs, and support them throughout their care.
* **Growth and capacity.** Grow completed visits and procedures by strengthening relationships with referring providers, making it easy to refer patients, and keeping referring offices informed. Convert more referrals into completed visits and procedures through timely scheduling, better use of clinic and ASC capacity, and fewer avoidable cancellations.
* **Stronger financial performance.** Labor and supply costs managed to budget, with timely resolution of operational issues affecting collections.
* **Less manual work and clearer accountability.** Use technology and automation to simplify workflows. Set clear ownership for follow-up and use data to track whether changes improve performance and hold over time.

**Preferred**

* Experience in physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, or another regulated service environment.
* Experience coordinating operations across locations or across teams with distinct professional responsibilities.

**Candidates from outside healthcare are encouraged to apply.** Leadership experience and a record of improving operations are essential. Physician practice management experience is optional.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

* **Stronger financial performance.** Labor and supply costs managed to budget, with timely resolution of operational issues affecting collections.
* **Less manual work and clearer accountability.** Use technology and automation to simplify workflows. Set clear ownership for follow-up and use data to track whether changes improve performance and hold over time.

**Preferred**

* Experience in physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, or another regulated service environment.
* Experience coordinating operations across locations or across teams with distinct professional responsibilities.

**Candidates from outside healthcare are encouraged to apply.** Leadership experience and a record of improving operations are essential. Physician practice management experience is optional.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

card.title: Operations Director
card.description:
**Job Summary**

As Operations Director, you’ll guide daily operations and strategic planning to help the organization deliver reliable service and meet its business goals. You’ll lead managers and teams, connect operational priorities with financial performance, and use data to identify opportunities for improvement. Your impact: By strengthening processes and aligning teams around clear priorities, you help customers receive consistent service and employees work effectively.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operations management, business management, and executive-level team management across relevant functions.
* Oversee financial management, profit and loss (P&L) analysis, and sales performance; use Excel data analysis to inform decisions.
* Set strategic plans and operational priorities, applying data-driven decision making and lean management principles.
* Direct project management and process improvement efforts, tracking progress and addressing barriers.
* Build team leadership and development practices, support customer service, and communicate priorities clearly to managers and staff.

**Requirements**

* Experience in operations management, supervising, and team management, with demonstrated leadership and managerial communication.
* Skills in financial management, P&L oversight, and profit and loss analysis; ability to interpret data in Excel.
* Knowledge of strategic management, strategic planning, project management, and process improvement.
* Ability to develop teams, lead managers, and balance operational priorities with sales and customer service.
* Lean management experience is preferred.

Pay: $225,000.00 - $245,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Referral program
* Relocation assistance
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Brentwood, TN 37027
